intro: You can create a coaching institute website without WordPress or a developer by using a hosted academy platform: pick a theme, edit the text, colours and logo, add your courses with prices, connect your own domain and publish. Hosting, security updates, course pages, student login and UPI checkout come built in, so there are no plugins to install or patch.

Maybe you run a JEE and NEET centre in Kota with three batches and a WhatsApp number painted on the board. Maybe you teach spoken English or yoga online, and a cousin once set up a WordPress site that now shows an update warning every time you log in. Either way, students ask the same three questions before they join: what do you teach, what does it cost, and how do I pay. A good coaching website answers all three on a phone, in under a minute.

This guide covers the pages a coaching website needs, the build steps, how course pages get found on Google, how payments work, the legal pages to add, what it costs, and when WordPress is still the better choice. If you want a full academy with courses, tests and live classes, read how to start an online academy in 5 steps alongside it.

sections.h2: Why build a coaching website without WordPress?
sections.html:
Because a coaching website is not just pages: it has to sell courses, take payments, log students in and play videos, and on WordPress each of those is a separate plugin or service you must set up and keep updated. A hosted academy platform does those jobs in one place, so the educator only works on content.

WordPress is a good, widely used tool. W3Techs reports that WordPress is used by 58.2% of websites whose content management system it can identify, which is 39.5% of all websites (October 2026).1 The software is free. The work is in what you add around it.

{{fig:wordpress-stack-vs-studio|A coaching institute website on WordPress needs hosting, a theme and page builder, an LMS plugin, a payment plugin, video hosting, security, updates and a separate app, while a hosted academy studio has all of it in one login|The WordPress stack for a coaching site, and the one-studio version.}}

The updates row is the one most educators underestimate. WordPress's own documentation says "You should always update WordPress to the latest version",2 and its security handbook starts its plugin advice with "make sure your plugins are always updated".3 That is sound advice, and it is also a recurring job. When a plugin update breaks the checkout during admission season, someone has to fix it.

We run this marketing site ourselves as a hand-maintained static site, so we know first-hand how many small jobs any website creates: titles, schema, sitemaps, image sizes, mobile checks. We built AllCoaching because a physics teacher should not have to learn domain settings, payment gateways and plugin updates to teach online.

sections.h2: What pages does a coaching institute website need?
sections.html:
A coaching institute website needs seven pages: a home page, course pages with prices, an about-the-teacher page, a results page only if your results are real, free content, a contact page with WhatsApp, and policy pages. Everything else is optional at the start.

{{fig:pages-anatomy|The seven pages a coaching institute website needs: home, courses with prices, about the teacher, results, free content, contact with WhatsApp and policies|Seven pages, shown as one illustrative coaching site. Names and prices are examples.}}

1. Home

Say who you teach, what, and in which language in the first line: "NEET Biology in Hindi for Class 11 and 12". Add one button to your courses and your WhatsApp number. A student should know within five seconds whether this site is for them.

2. Courses with prices

One page per course: who it is for, what is inside (lessons, PDFs, tests, live classes), validity, language, price and a buy button. Hiding the price behind "call for fees" costs you the students who browse at 11 pm and never call. Our guide to pricing online courses in India helps you set it.

3. About the teacher

A clear photo, your years of teaching, the exams or skills you cover, and your method in plain words. Parents read this page more carefully than any other.

4. Results, only if real

Show selections, scores or student reviews only when they are real, recent and shared with the student's permission. Borrowed topper photos and invented numbers damage trust the moment a parent checks. If you are new, skip this page and let free content do the work.

5. Free content

A free demo lesson, a chapter PDF or a short test lets a student judge your teaching before paying. It also gives Google something useful to index.

6. Contact and WhatsApp

A WhatsApp button that opens a chat in one tap, a phone number, your centre's address and a map if you teach offline. Many Indian students will message before they buy.

7. Policies

Privacy policy, terms of use and a refund policy, linked in the footer. More on these in the legal pages section below.

{{q:Should I put student testimonials on my coaching website?|Yes, if they are real. Ask the student in writing, use their actual words, and add their exam and year. A short WhatsApp message from a real student, shared with permission, builds more trust than a polished quote nobody can verify. Never write testimonials yourself or reuse photos of toppers from other institutes.}}

sections.h2: How does a coaching website get found on Google?
sections.html:
A coaching website gets found on Google through clear course pages that match what students type, a plain title and description on every page, structured data, and helpful free content that links to your courses. You do not need plugins for any of this.

Start with the course page. Name it the way students search: "SSC CGL Maths Course in Hindi", not "Batch 7 Premium". Google's documentation explains that it "uses structured data that it finds on the web to understand the content of the page".4 On WordPress, that usually means another SEO plugin. On AllCoaching, every course page gets SEO meta and schema when you save the course, and the academy-wide SEO title, description and sharing image sit in the studio's preferences.

  • One page per course, with the exam, subject and language in the title.
  • Syllabus as text, not an image, so Google and students can read it.
  • A short FAQ on each course page answering validity, language and doubt support.
  • Blog posts that answer exam questions (syllabus, cut-offs, study plans) and link to the course.
  • A Google Business Profile if you also teach from a physical centre.

Our SEO guide for online academies goes deeper into keywords, site structure and AI search.

sections.h2: How do students pay on a coaching website?
sections.html:
Students pay through a checkout on your course page: they choose UPI or card, the payment gateway confirms it, course access opens, and the money is paid out to your bank. No payment screenshots, no manual adding to groups.

On WordPress this means a payment plugin, a gateway account, and testing that the two keep working after every update. On AllCoaching, UPI and card checkout through Razorpay is built in, and payouts go to your bank automatically. The gateway still verifies you once with PAN and bank details, and its charges on student payments are separate from your plan. Coupons and lead forms are included for launch offers and enquiries.

Before you share the site, buy one of your own courses with UPI on your phone. It is the fastest way to catch a confusing step. Our guide to accepting UPI payments for online courses lists the documents and charges.

sections.h2: Why a coaching website must be mobile-first
sections.html:
Your students, especially in tier-2 and tier-3 towns, will open your website on a phone, often an inexpensive Android phone on mobile data, and Google also judges your site by its mobile version. Design and check for the phone first, then the laptop.

Google Search Central puts it plainly: "Google uses the mobile version of a site's content, crawled with the smartphone agent, for indexing and ranking."5 If your course details or prices are hidden on the phone view, Google may not see them either.

{{fig:mobile-first|Mobile-first checklist for a coaching institute website, shown next to the Biology Lessons academy website on a phone|Eight checks for the phone view. Phone screen: Biology Lessons, an academy on AllCoaching.}}

Open your site on the oldest phone in your family, on mobile data. Can you read the text without zooming? Is the price easy to find? Does WhatsApp open in one tap? Can you pay by UPI without getting lost? If a Hindi-medium student is your audience, are the key lines in Hindi?

The next step on a phone is an app. Students who study daily come back more easily from an icon than a bookmark. Every AllCoaching plan includes your own Android app, published on your own Play Store account, and the iOS app is included on Pro monthly and every yearly plan. On WordPress, an app is a separate project.

sections.h2: Which legal pages does a coaching website need?
sections.html:
Before you sell, add a privacy policy, terms of use, a refund and cancellation policy, and a contact page with your real name, address, phone and email. Payment gateways often ask for these pages when they review your website, and parents look for the refund policy before paying a large fee.

  • Privacy policy: what student data you collect (name, phone, email, payments), why, and how a student can ask you to correct or delete it. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 applies to how you handle that data.
  • Terms of use: course validity, account sharing, recording rules and what happens if a batch is rescheduled.
  • Refund and cancellation policy: whether refunds are possible, within how many days, and how to ask. Clear rules prevent most disputes.
  • Contact: a real address and phone number. A website with only a form looks less trustworthy than one with a person behind it.

Create these as normal pages with the page builder and link them in the footer. Have a lawyer or CA review them once; a template copied from another institute may promise things you do not do.

sections.h2: When does WordPress still make sense for a coaching institute?
sections.html:
WordPress still makes sense if you already have a developer who maintains it, if your site is mainly a large blog or news publication, or if you need a specific plugin no academy platform offers. It is a flexible tool; the question is whether you want to run it yourself.

WordPress fits when

  • A developer or agency already maintains your site and you are happy with it.
  • Your site is mostly articles, news or exam updates, with few paid courses.
  • You need a niche plugin or custom feature for your institute.
  • You enjoy managing hosting, themes and updates yourself.

A hosted academy fits when

  • You want to sell courses, tests and live classes, not only publish pages.
  • Nobody on your team wants to handle updates and security.
  • You want your own Android app without a separate project.
  • You want one login for website, payments, students and content.

A middle path also works: keep an existing WordPress site for news and articles, and link its "Courses" button to your academy for courses, payments and student login. When you are ready to move everything, copy your page text across, bulk-import your students from Excel or Google Sheet, recreate important course URLs where it makes sense, and point your domain at the academy.

faq: Can I create a coaching institute website without WordPress?

Yes. A hosted academy platform gives you themes, pages, course pages, student login and UPI checkout in one place. You pick a theme, edit the text, colours and logo, add your courses, connect your domain and publish, with no WordPress, plugins or hosting to manage.
Do I need a developer to build a coaching website?

No. On a hosted academy platform you edit pages visually, course pages are created when you save a course, and connecting a domain means copying DNS records at your registrar. A developer is only needed if you want custom features the platform does not offer.
What pages should a coaching institute website have?

Seven: a home page that says who you teach, course pages with prices, an about-the-teacher page, a results page only if your results are real, free content such as a demo lesson, a contact page with WhatsApp, and privacy, terms and refund policy pages.
Is WordPress free for a coaching website?

The WordPress software is free, but a coaching site on it also needs hosting, a domain, usually a premium theme or page builder, an LMS plugin, a payment plugin and regular updates. Those costs and the maintenance time are separate.

Will my coaching website show up on Google?

Can I use my own domain for my coaching website?

Can I get a mobile app with my coaching website?

Yes. Every AllCoaching plan includes your own Android app published on your own Play Store account, and the iOS app is included on Pro monthly and every yearly plan. On WordPress, an app is usually a separate project.
